cast.bio: Miharu is a vampire with beautiful manners, formal speech, and absolutely no sense of what is appropriate to say out loud. She is very old, very polite, and will announce the most alarming thing in the room in the same tone she uses to offer tea.

cast.name: Nemu Miyao
cast.role: A witch who specializes in shape-shifting
cast.bio: Nemu is a witch who specializes in shape-shifting, which she uses for pranks far more often than for anything useful. Sleepy, deadpan, and a menace.

title: Yona of the Dawn
hook: If you want a main character who starts out useless and does not stay that way.
description: A sheltered princess watches her father get killed and has to run for her life with one bodyguard. She goes from useless to genuinely dangerous over the course of the show, mostly by learning to shoot a bow and refusing to quit.
about:
Yona is a princess who has never had to do anything. She is sixteen, she cares about her hair, and her biggest problem is that her father will not let her marry her cousin. Then, on her birthday, she watches that cousin kill her father and take the throne, and she escapes into the night with one bodyguard and nothing else.

What follows is a survival story that turns into a quest. She learns to walk long distances. She learns to shoot a bow, badly at first, and then well. She finds out what the kingdom is actually like outside the palace — which is poor, hungry and being sold off — and she starts collecting the people she needs to do something about it, including four warriors out of an old legend.

The reason this one gets recommended is Yona herself. She starts genuinely useless and the show does not shortcut her out of it; she gets competent slowly, through work, and keeps the softness she started with.

The politics are more complicated than they first look — the cousin who did it is not a simple villain and the show refuses to make him one.

cast.name: Yona
cast.role: A sheltered princess forced to run for her life
cast.bio: Yona goes from a sheltered princess who has never carried anything to a fighter who can put an arrow through a target at distance, and the transition is earned rather than granted. She is stubborn, emotionally direct, and refuses to let anyone protect her from what her country actually looks like. She keeps the red hair her father loved and everyone else calls unlucky.

cast.name: Hak Son
cast.role: Her bodyguard, and former general of the Wind Tribe
cast.bio: Hak was the youngest general of the Wind Tribe and Yona's bodyguard since childhood, and he is the single most dangerous person in the group with a glaive. He deflects everything with sarcasm, bullies Yona relentlessly, and would walk into a burning building for her without breaking stride. He is not going to say any of that out loud.

cast.name: Yun
cast.role: The group's healer, sharp-tongued and very capable
cast.bio: Yun is not a fighter and says so at every opportunity. He is the group's healer, cook, negotiator and quartermaster, raised by a traveling priest, and he is sharper than anyone else in the party. He calls himself a beautiful genius, and he is not entirely wrong.

cast.name: Ki-Ja
cast.role: The White Dragon, with one enormously powerful arm
cast.bio: Ki-Ja is the White Dragon, born with one enormous clawed arm strong enough to tear through armor. He was raised in a village that treated him as a sacred object, so he is formal, dramatic and desperate to be useful. Easily flustered, especially by Hak.

cast.name: Shin-Ah
cast.role: The Blue Dragon, who can see for miles
cast.bio: Shin-Ah is the Blue Dragon, who can see for miles and whose eyes do something to anyone who meets them, which is why he has spent his life in a mask and mostly alone. He barely speaks. He is enormously gentle, and the arc of him learning that he is allowed to be around people is the quiet heart of the group.

cast.name: Jae-Ha
cast.role: The Green Dragon, who can leap almost like flying
cast.bio: Jae-Ha is the Green Dragon, whose leg lets him leap high enough that it looks like flight. He spent years running from the legend that says he has to serve a king, and he joins on his own terms and keeps saying so. Charming, lazy, and much more serious underneath.
